q: How many Alsace grand cru sites exist, and which was added last (2007)?
exp: Each grand cru is its own AOP since 2011.

q: Alsace has a trio of grand crus permitted to grow non-noble white varieties by exception. Name any one.
exp: The noble-grape rule bends here — and separately, Pinot Noir now makes red Alsace Grand Cru at Hengst and Kirchberg de Barr (from 2022), joined by Vorbourg in 2024.

q: Which producer's Clos Sainte-Hune, from grand cru Rosacker, is Alsace's most celebrated Riesling?
exp: ~1.67 ha; Trimbach declines to print the grand cru name on principle.

q: Which grand cru, at Thann on volcanic-sedimentary rock, holds Zind-Humbrecht's monopole clos?
exp: Alsace's southernmost, steepest grand cru — smoky Pinot Gris and Riesling.

q: Vendanges Tardives minimum must weights are set per variety. Which two varieties carry the higher bar?
ans: Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris (higher); Riesling and Muscat (lower)
exp: VT: 235 g/L for Riesling and Muscat, 257 g/L for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris; SGN: 276 and 306 g/L respectively.

q: What does 'Gentil' on an Alsace label require?
accept: blend majority noble grapes vinified separately
ans: A blend with ≥50% noble varieties, each vinified separately
exp: Edelzwicker is the freer blend term, any proportion, no separate vinification.

q: Which house's 'Cuvée Frédéric Émile' Riesling draws from grands crus Geisberg and Osterberg?
exp: Trimbach again — labeled without the cru names, per house doctrine.

q: Crémant d'Alsace's rosé must be 100% of which grape?
exp: The only red of Alsace; still versions increasingly serious (Rouge d'Ottrott, Saint-Hippolyte).

q: The Alsace bottle shape, protected by law, is called:
ans: The flûte d'Alsace (Vin du Rhin bottle)
exp: Mandatory for AOP Alsace still wines.

q: Domaine Weinbach farms beneath which grand cru, its labels bearing the Clos des Capucins?
exp: The Faller women built its modern fame; granite Riesling of chiseled charm.

q: Name three Alsace grand crus and a producer associated with each.
accept: rangen zind-humbrecht schlossberg weinbach brand josmeyer hengst barmes
ans: e.g., Rangen (Zind-Humbrecht), Schlossberg (Weinbach), Hengst (Josmeyer/Barmès-Buecher), Brand, Geisberg, Sommerberg
exp: Producer-to-cru pairing is the Advanced form of this question.

q: What geological feature makes Rangen unique among Alsace grands crus?
ans: Volcanic-sedimentary rock on a ~90% slope above the Thur — the only truly volcanic grand cru
exp: It gives Pinot Gris and Riesling a smoky, almost gunflint intensity.

q: Explain Alsace's political history and its effect on wine style.
accept: passed between france and germany bulk production then quality
ans: Passed between France and Germany repeatedly (1871, 1918, 1940, 1945); German-era bulk demands delayed the quality focus until the AOC of 1962
exp: Which is why grand crus arrived only in 1975 — late for such a historic region.

q: Which Alsace village names appear most often on labels of note (name three)?
accept: riquewihr ribeauville turckheim hunawihr bergheim ammerschwihr
ans: e.g., Riquewihr, Ribeauvillé, Turckheim, Hunawihr, Bergheim, Ammerschwihr
exp: Village recognition anchors the cru map.

ans: Zwicker was the basic blend (now obsolete); Edelzwicker is the 'noble' blend term still in use
exp: Gentil is the stricter modern successor at ≥50% noble varieties.

q: AOC Alsace Grand Cru caps yields well below the regional appellation. Its base yield is:
exp: Alsace Grand Cru is set at 55 hl/ha, against 80 hl/ha for white AOC Alsace, with Vendanges Tardives and Sélection de Grains Nobles lower still. The number is worth carrying because it is the heart of the case against the system: 55 hl/ha is generous for a top tier, the serious growers work at half of it voluntarily, and the law does not oblige anyone to. A hierarchy that does not bite on yield is a hierarchy the market is entitled to distrust.
